# mcrl trace

## mcrl trace get

Show the spans of a trace.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl trace get <trace-id>

Aliases:
  get, show

Show the spans of a trace as an array, in the API's format.

API: GET /api/v0/traces/<id>
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl trace get 5b8efff798038103d269b633813fc60c
  mcrl trace get 5b8efff798038103d269b633813fc60c --jq '.[] | [.name, .startTime, .endTime] | @tsv'
```

## mcrl trace list

Search traces.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl trace list --service <service> [flags]

Aliases:
  list, ls

Search traces of a service, newest first (or by latency with --sort latency).
The time range is at most 30 minutes (the API's limit).

--attr and --resource-attr take conditions like "http.route=/users/{id}" or
"http.response.status_code>=500", with the type inferred from the value.

API: POST /api/v0/traces
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl trace list --service web --status error
  mcrl trace list --service web --since 1h --min-latency 1s --sort latency --jq '.[] | [.traceId, .traceLatencyMillis, .title] | @tsv'

Flags:
      --asc                         ascending order
      --attr stringArray            span attribute condition (repeatable)
      --env string                  deployment environment
      --issue string                issue fingerprint
      --limit int                   maximum number of traces (0 = all) (default 20)
      --max-latency string          maximum latency
      --min-latency string          minimum latency, e.g. "500ms", "2s"
      --namespace string            service namespace
      --resource-attr stringArray   resource attribute condition (repeatable)
      --service string              service name (required)
      --since string                start of the time range (default "15m")
      --sort string                 start or latency (default "start")
      --span-name string            span name
      --status string               ok or error
      --trace-id string             trace ID
      --until string                end of the time range (default "now")
      --version string              service version
```
